# THE KEPT WORLD — creative direction C for the whole site

2026-09-03 · Direction for the film body (stages 1–8), the persistent interface, and the
endcard. Anchored on the shipped hero (`src/film/stages/hero.ts`, `trilayer.ts`,
`rigs.ts`, `heroLife.ts` — verified, P5-REVIEW) and on the locked law: `story.md`,
`copy-spec.md`, the three 2026-09-02 system docs. Everything here extends what already
passed review; nothing here re-litigates it.

---

## 0. Position — what this direction claims

The hero proved the *techniques*. It did not yet name the *idea that scales them*. A
drafting-table reading stages the film on a desk — a frame around the world. A
travelling-seam reading walks the hero's paint frontier through the film — a wipe
stretched to nine minutes; by stage 4 the trick is spent and stages 5–8 are back to
"apply trilayer everywhere."

This direction's claim: the organizing idea is already inside the locked script, waiting
to be excavated. Scene 1 is *"he is literally preparing tomorrow's adventure."* The
ending bookend is the cliff **tended** — remains cleared, a cairn, three mushrooms
planted (`world.ts:4052–4093` already builds it). And the film's most product-forward
line is `pitch1`: *"I've built worlds for your DM for years."*

**The years must be visible.** Not as a metaphor layered on top — as texture, in every
surface, provable by the time the line is lettered on.

---

## 1. Core concept

**Every surface in this film is a document of its keeping — drawn, painted, worn,
erased, and re-painted by one goblin, for years — and the freeze is when you're allowed
to read the file.**

Why this is true for THIS product and no other: a DM's campaign world is exactly a
long-kept document. The map gets redrawn between sessions, the tavern gets reused, the
encounter gets rebalanced, the eraser ghosts stay in the paper. Good Goblin's pitch is
taking over that upkeep — *build the maps, run the table, the goblin does the rest*. A
generic product can claim a maker; only a DM tool can claim a **keeper**. The film's
ending (the tended cliff), its thesis proof (light as someone's nightly work), and its
climax caption ("for years") are all already about maintenance. The art direction's job
is to make the pixels agree.

Three tenses, one trilayer (the shipped material already carries all three —
`trilayer.ts:5–27`):

| Layer | Tense | What it says |
|---|---|---|
| **Underdrawing** (Prep) | past — how it was decided | construction, measure ticks, *and the revisions*: erased lines, ghost positions, scribed arcs. The pentimento layer. The hero already ships one erased-and-redrawn line (hero doc §4); the film promotes that single stroke to a language. |
| **Paint** (Performance) | present — how it plays | committed gouache, the current coat, the world the players will get tomorrow |
| **Wear** | continuous — whose hands keep it | drybrush on handled corners, rubbed paint where he always jumps down, the ruts between islands |

Discipline (what keeps this from becoming clutter — the one-subject rule is law): the
film carries exactly **four flagship evidence beats**, one per proof plus the bookend —
S2's erased cliff contour, S4's scribed arcs under the stage disc, S5's graphite mug
rings on the tavern table, S7's tended cairn. Everything else is second-plane texture,
discoverable on scrub-back, never the eye-path. Evidence whispers; it never captions
itself.

---

## 2. Narrative — an argument you can audit

The claim–three-proofs–handover shape (direction doc §2) stands. What THE KEPT WORLD
adds is that each stage argues in a different **tense of keeping**, so the film builds a
case instead of a reel:

1. **The Claim (S1)** — the shared memory, inverted. The ambush aftermath is already
   evidence: dropped kit, arrows in rock, a fire someone laid. The audience just doesn't
   know whose work it is yet.
2. **The Address (S2)** — the file opens. First freeze, first underdrawing, first
   revision mark, the grid — the oldest layer of all. "You thought I ran away" lands
   over proof that this world was *decided*, not found.
3. **Proof of light (S3)** — present tense: tonight's shift. Every prop beat leaves the
   world more alive than he found it.
4. **Proof of scenery (S4)** — past-perfect: the infrastructure. The freeze-flicker
   shows machinery **worn by years of use** — the disc has swung ten thousand times.
5. **Proof of time (S5)** — the intervention. The freeze shows the table's own history
   (mug rings in graphite): this room has hosted years of the game the die is about to
   save.
6. **The many jobs (S6)** — habitual tense. Six vignettes of routine; silent, because
   routine doesn't announce itself.
7. **The handover (S7)** — the verdict. By the time `pitch1` writes on, the visitor has
   *already seen* the years — the line reads as a conclusion they reached, not a claim
   they're asked to trust. The flatten then reveals the ledger the work was kept in: the
   map.
8. **The Table (S8)** — the ledger is handed over, and it is the product.

All twelve captions verbatim per `copy-spec.md`. No new words anywhere — the evidence
layer is marks only (ticks, numerals via `pencil.ts`'s `numeral()`, arrows, erasures),
never lettering.

## 3. Visual world — islands, and the tissue between them

Islands-on-the-page is binding (direction §3) and the hero built the recipe: elliptical
card over a solid three-band lathe skirt (earth lip / darkened stone shelf / caveDark
keel), bent tapering roots, a drawn rim contour that stops being drawn
(`hero.ts`, ASSETS.md `island-card` — verified at four breakpoints). The film's seven
sets are that recipe at set scale. Two additions:

- **The edge is a section through the layers.** At every island's cut edge, the paint
  reads as a *thin skin* over the sectioned earth — a bright 2–3px painted lip over the
  strata, the way a painted maquette shows its build at the cut. The world is painted
  *on*, thinly, exactly as the trilayer doctrine says — and the island edge is where the
  film admits it. (The hero's skirt already splits painted/graphite section lines per
  side; the film inherits that.)
- **Places relate by wear, not by roads alone.** The connective tissue between islands
  is the keeper's traffic: cart ruts entering at the island edge and stopping where the
  pencil line stops, a rubbed patch where he always lands, the worn path the hero's
  albedo bake already authors (`bakeIslandAlbedo`'s path + ruts). The film's world map
  is legible as *his commute*.

The page: the margin system of experience §4, unchanged — sheet, ticks, penciled C1…C7,
66-tick ruler, whisper/breathe. The page is where the film's oldest layer (the grid)
lives; the grid ghost stays ≤4% ink (`GRID_INK`, `trilayer.ts:31`, sandbox-asserted).

---

## 4. Typography

Three voices, binding per direction §4 + hero amendment §14.4. This direction's rulings
on drawn-vs-live and on discipline:

1. **The Hand** — the twelve captions + endcard tagline, authored stroke SVGs in the
   wordmark's hand, write-on/un-write, graphite in Prep, ink in Performance. **The Hand
   never revises.** The world carries erasures; the narrator does not — his voice is the
   one confident thing in the film. No boil on captions mid-write; boil only at rest.
2. **The Inscription** — Cinzel 700 caps: the CTA and the three wayfinding labels. Nothing
   else, ever.
3. **The Quiet Serif** — Vollkorn: subline, meta, skip note, © line.
4. **Drawn art vs live text:** every lettered caption ships with real text in the DOM —
   the SR document (experience §9) is the film's canonical transcript, first in DOM,
   with the twelve lines verbatim + scene sentences + the endcard copy and real link.
   The endcard tagline/subline/CTA are live DOM text (selectable, indexable) styled by
   halo, not baked pixels. The wordmark is art with an accessible name. SEO reads the
   page; the canvas is `aria-hidden`.
5. **Marks are not type.** The evidence layer's numerals and ticks come from
   `pencil.ts`'s stroke primitives (`numeral()`, `polyline()`), not from any font — they
   are drawing furniture and are never asked to be read as language.

## 5. Color palette — the committed tokens, plus two laws of age

The palette is shipped and structured (`palette.ts` — v2 spine + alive ramp + frozen v1
world tokens). Exact values, with their governing discipline:

**The spine:** paper `#F7F5F0` · ink `#222222` · tooth `#E8E5DF` · graphiteLight
`#B9B6B0` · graphite `#82807A` · graphiteDark `#4A4844`. Near-zero chroma by
adjudication (`palette.ts:27–29`) — no cream drift, no parchment tokens; parchment
warmth belongs to the curtain shader alone.

**The alive ramp — the only glow:** amber `#F2C35E` → amberLantern `#E8963E` →
amberEmber `#C75B2A`, key light `keyWarm #FFEACC` (a light color, not a glow). One open
violation to retire: `Film.tsx:100` still parents a `0xffb45e` point light into the
flame groups (ledgered as P3-T6) — the film-body rebuild replaces it with the amber
ramp.

**The world:** the frozen chapter tokens — skyDusk `#6D78AE`, skyDay `#ACCDE6`,
skyOvercast `#AAB6C0`, skyHearth `#D4B184`, skyVellum `#EEE6D2`, skyDawn `#E6C1A2`,
skyBoard `#F7F5F0`; grounds/foliage/wood/fire/cloth/metal tokens as shipped. Storybook
gouache: mixed, muted, committed mids, airy lights.

**The goblin:** goblinGreen `#84A058` skin, olive cloak ramp, amber eyes. Green is his
alone. wordmarkPip `#B6D648` on the die pip and nowhere else.

Two new laws, both scoped so they cannot re-bleach the film (the colour pass explicitly
fought its way out of pale washes — `palette.ts:1–11`):

- **Age is thinness, never yellow.** An older coat sits closer to paper (more tooth
  show-through), same hue, never warmer — the no-parchment ruling applies to time
  itself. Capped: thinness is an *accent* on ≤15% of any surface (worn centers, rubbed
  edges); the mass tone keeps the committed grade.
- **A repair is one step off.** A repainted patch may sit exactly one value step from
  its ground, same hue family, edges drybrushed — visible to a reader, invisible to a
  scanner. Repairs never introduce a hue.

Contrast floors binding: captions ≥4.5:1, grid ≤4% ink, interface ink ≥3:1 breathed.

## 6. Composition — storyboard discipline, plus the evidence plane

Binding from direction §6: four-plane rule, one eye-path per shot, goblin on thirds
(dead-center only for the two direct addresses), captions in the lower-third band on the
margin system, page margin instead of letterboxing, portrait restack + 70° FOV clamp.

Additions:

- **Evidence lives in plane two or four, never plane three.** The keeping marks ride the
  foreground occluder (a graphite tuft, a rope) or the supporting element — never the
  subject. If an evidence mark competes with the beat's subject, the mark moves.
- **The four flagship beats get the subject slot** exactly once each, inside a freeze,
  where the world is silent and the eye has nowhere else to be (S2 contour, S4 arcs, S5
  rings, S7 cairn — the cairn is already scripted as the shot).
- **Phone truth-test:** every flagship evidence read must survive 390px width or demote
  itself to texture. The hero's own ledger proves the method (comp re-solved per
  breakpoint, measured, P4e) — the film's islands take the same height-aware solve, and
  the S5 mug rings, sized like the die's numerals, are QA'd at 390 exactly as the die
  faces are (clarity contract §11.5).
- **The camera never hunts evidence.** No insert shots, no push-ins onto marks. You find
  the arcs because you scrubbed back; the film never says "look."

## 7. Materials — the trilayer, extended to every class

One material, two truths, per surface (`trilayer.ts` — curtain-mixed, seam-capable,
sheet-basis param space, authored stroke-tile bake). The hero's four proven techniques
are the toolkit: **canvas-baked gouache albedo** (`bakeIslandAlbedo` — committed dabs in
measured value tiers), **baked stroke tiles** for graphite tone (`bakeStrokeTiles` —
four density tiers of hand-drawn tapered strokes, one family direction, flipY=false,
anisotropy 16), **the 4-tier tone quantizer** (P4d, unchanged under P4e), and
**anisotropic dab noise** at frontiers (the seam study — ASSETS.md's "cleanest win").
Per class:

| Class | Paint (Performance) | Underdrawing (Prep) | Wear |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rock / cliff** | baked gouache in 3 quantized tiers riding the roughen; strata section bands at cuts (hero skirt recipe) | authored contour arcs + sectioned strata lines; stroke-tile tone via sheet basis (one direction per mass — the P4e fix that killed the swirl) | drybrush on the climbable edges only — rock wears where hands go |
| **Timber / carpentry** | `bakeBark`-family directional streak bake along the grain; straight edges kept (carpentry is carpentry) | box construction + end-arcs + strap lines (the chest's `boxMarks` pattern) | corner-lightening on handled parts: door ring, bench ends, rope-worn kerb |
| **Foliage** | `bakeFoliage` clump-mass tiles on lobed-crown / tiered-cone geometry; paint-side posterizer (uTriPoster ≈12) for committed steps | scalloped lobe outlines + interior leaf arcs; zigzag fir silhouettes **derived from the cone profile** (`silR()` — the P4e lesson: never author silhouette radii free) | none — trees are tended, not handled |
| **Cloth** | fold-following brushwork, one direction per garment panel; committed shadow mass | contour + two fold lines, no tone fill on small cloth | hem-edge drybrush (the goblin's cloak hem, bedroll edge) |
| **Water** | flat pigment band + tangent-aligned lit dabs; **shorelines take the seam's anisotropic dab frontier** — drybrush where water meets land | **water is left as bare paper with a drawn edge line.** A pencil doesn't fill water; the drawing admits it. (Retires `world.ts:4260`'s hatch water.) | none |
| **Metal** | gouache by value (brass/iron tokens), matte; **one authored glint stroke** per hero prop — the die's technique, never specular | contour + a single core-shadow stroke | rubbed-bright on gripped parts (lantern handle, door ring) |
| **Fire / light** | lathe tongue geometry + `buildGlowSprite` amber radial + painted glow cones; the only emissive family | a still graphite teardrop — drawn flame, no glow, no rays | scorch as *painted* dark pooling, not crosshatch (retires `world.ts:1595–1606`, `4016–4044`) |
| **Snow** | **reserved paper.** Snow is the page showing through, shaped by blue-grey shadow strokes and a drawn windward edge — you paint around snow, not over it. Makes the C3 mountain flat doctrinally beautiful and nearly free | already a drawing — snow's Prep state is its Performance state minus the shadow strokes | none |
| **Paper props** (sheets, sign faces, DM screen, book) | dieBone ground + authored illegible scribble-rows, one direction (retires every `hatch()` "writing": `world.ts:2147, 2189, 3249, 3277, 3866`) | the same scribble in graphite | dog-eared corner lightening |
| **The painted map** (S7 flatten targets, S8 board) | the product's own art: flat map paint for terrain, inked roads, painted flame marks, token discs — authored as a real Good Goblin map | the grid — the map's underdrawing IS the battle grid, which is the film's whole point | the board shows light handling wear at its edges: this map has been played on |

**The hatch retirement program** is a named work item, not a side effect: 34
`hatch()`/`crossHatch()` call sites remain in `world.ts` (goblin flank/jaw/cloak
978/1211/1366, cave mouth 1941, tavern night/firebox 3018/3059, montage tones, cliff
cracks/scorches, miniature fields/water). Every one maps to a row above. The
`curtain.ts` shader's near-black hatch accent goes with them.

## 8. Lighting — two rigs, one ledger

The shipped rigs (`stages/rigs.ts`) carry the whole film: Performance = warm key + sky
fill + amber practicals with token-driven flicker; Prep = flat paper light, **no shadows
— a drawing casts none** — except the alive (goblin + touched, `rig.aliveShadow`,
promoted to a uniform at P4e so stages can commit it).

Per-chapter scripts, finally honored, driven by the frozen sky tokens:

| Stage | Air | Key | The one rule applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | skyDusk indigo — real night | the campfire, sole warm pool; embers | the film's first proof that light is painted |
| S2 | Prep | none — paper light | his shadow is the only one in the frame |
| S3 | Prep → skyDay morning | the lantern he lights; the key warms as the world returns | color arrives *with* shadows, from the touch point |
| S4 | skyOvercast — stage-lit-by-nothing | flat gray key, no practicals | a theatre between shows; the flicker's graphite machinery casts nothing |
| S5 | skyHearth interior | lamplight pools, dark corners; candle + hearth practicals | the film's only interior; warmth is the room's argument |
| S6 | skyVellum — bright, flat, weightless | one soft key per vignette | montage light never changes mid-vignette |
| S7 | skyDawn gold | low dawn key + painted god-ray cones | light is a painted object, never a flare |
| S8 | skyBoard = paper | none; the board is lit by the page | the film ends in the light it was drawn in |

**The lantern ledger (new rule):** every light source in the film is one the goblin lit
on camera or plausibly maintains — fire he laid, lanterns he filled, candles he set
(S6's sixth vignette is literally him lighting them). No unmotivated light anywhere.
Light is his signature; that's why the CTA taking light on touch reads as *his* grammar
handed to you.

One shipped violation retires with the rebuild: the non-amber `0xffb45e` glow
(`Film.tsx:100`, P3-T6).

## 9. 3D elements — the kit register

Build once, reuse everywhere. Hero tier gets the die's polish budget; set tier gets the
island recipe; grammar tier is uniforms and marks, nearly free.

**Hero tier (jewel polish):**
- **The goblin** — full surface rebuild, §14 below (the client's named complaint).
- **The d20** — painted numerals, worn edges, one authored glint; real inertia; the
  nudge. Geometry solved (`dieGeometry.ts`); the treatment is the work. Also `die2` and
  the endcard send-off die.
- **The lantern kit** — lamppost (the hero's, restaged so the flame is never occluded by
  its own post — the P4d-T5 lesson is a *staging* rule now), hand lantern, campfire
  (ring + logs + tongue flames + glow), tavern hearth, candle set, ember/moth/mote
  particles.
- **The carpenter's pencil + the brush and pigment pot** — the keeper's tools. The
  pencil exists (hero); the brush + pot are new, live in the satchel, and appear in S6
  (roads vignette uses the fence-post pencil; the touch-up grammar uses the brush). They
  are the trilayer's origin story as props: pencil draws the Prep, brush paints the
  Performance.

**Set tier (the island recipe at set scale):**
- Seven chapter islands with sculpted three-band edges, roots, drawn rims: camp island
  (S1), cliff island (S1/S2/S7 — one asset, two eras of dressing), path ribbon island
  (S3 — the hero island's big sibling; the hero *is* a slice of it, so its bakes extend
  1:1), theatre disc + backstage apron (S4), tavern interior shell (S5), six vignette
  islets (S6), the miniature world (S7).
- Theatre machinery — capstan, radial rails, counterweights, the rope (catenary + fray +
  coil, shipped at `world.ts:2802+`) — graphite-only, freeze-visible, **worn**: scribed
  arcs on the under-disc where it has swung for years (flagship beat 2).
- The snowy mountain flat — reserved-paper snow, honest theatre flat.
- The final board — a real authored Good Goblin map (replaces the GridHelper + boardFill
  placeholder at `world.ts:4329+`).

**Cast tier (silhouette-first, never out-chroma the goblin):**
- Adventurer trio (S1, re-surfaced: painted cloaks, no interior hatch), the DM + two
  players (S5), tavern patrons, ravens (×3), the monster (S6 — its tick-stroke shag at
  `world.ts:3526` is already the right no-hatch language; keep, repaint).
- **The NPC as a based miniature** (S6 vignette 5): the script's own simile — "moving
  NPCs into villages like a chess piece" — made literal. A painted figure on a visible
  base is a token; at the flatten, all figures resolve to token discs. The product
  rhyme costs one prop.

**Keeping props (the concept's own shelf):** cairn stones + planted mushrooms (shipped,
`world.ts:4052+`), signpost with older nail holes in graphite, chest + judged coins,
tavern sign + chain, mugs (whose rings are on the table), bedroll/pack/spear camp kit,
arrows + dropped shield (S1 remains), eraser-ghost decals (graphite-layer marks: a
door's previous swing arc, a tree's prior position ellipse — four total, one per
flagship beat's supporting cast).

**Grammar tier:** underdrawing on every asset (trilayer, free), grid ghost per island,
margin furniture (ticks, numerals, ruler, skip note), particle language (motes, moths,
embers, cloud flats — Performance-only, frozen mid-air by the tick).

## 10. Depth — three cues, zero videogame

The two shipped languages are binding and already in-material (`trilayer.ts:15–21`):

- **Performance depth is atmospheric:** distance ramps the lit result toward PAPER
  (`rig.depthNear/depthFar`), never grey; parallax cloud/hill flats behind; tilt-shift
  DOF at exactly two moments (die close-up, C6 miniature reveal).
- **Prep depth is graphite:** no fog, no DOF — line-weight falloff, far strokes fainter
  with more paper; foreground occluders go near-black silhouette
  (`rig.silhouetteNear`).

The addition — **depth doubles as age:** because distance fades toward paper, far
scenery naturally reads as *older, thinner coats* and near scenery as the freshest
paint plus the most wear. The film's space and the film's time agree without a single
new uniform. The camera vocabulary stays authored rails, push-ins on freezes, the
angle-echo bookend, the axis-locked rise — no orbits, no free camera, ever.

---

## 11. Motion language — what the body does with the two clocks

Architecture is shipped and binding (`motion.ts` tokens, three ease lanes, the two
clocks, seven named transitions). The film body's dialect on top:

- **The keeping gestures are the choreography.** The acting alphabet
  (`actions.ts`: stoop, lift, tap, haul, shrug, wave, nudge, dustOff, straighten) grows
  four verbs, same file, puppet lane: **hang** (sign), **plant-and-pat** (tree),
  **coin-drop** (judged), **touch-up** (one brush stroke — used once, S6). His work
  reads as *practiced* — no gesture hesitates, every settle is `power2.out` confidence.
- **Touched things bank their life.** The S3 grammar (each revealed prop regains its
  idle, one by one — embers of motion accumulating in a still world) is the body's
  signature move; S6 reprises it per vignette at tempo.
- **The world only ever moves where he has been.** Ambient life (flicker, moths, leaf
  sway) rides `world.t` and exists only on surfaces he has lit or dressed — the lantern
  ledger, kinetically. An untouched graphite region is still by construction.
- **Freezes are instant; resumes exhale.** The tick (≤0.15t) and the exhale (0.3t) as
  catalogued; the t12.5 stop tightens to spec when S2 rebuilds (P1-T3/P2-T4).
- **The scrub reads backwards as un-keeping.** Reverse un-paints, un-writes, un-lights
  in reveal order — the projectionist can always audit the work. The flatten and the
  disc turn are the two must-be-flawless-both-ways moves.
- Reduced motion: the stepped picture book, per the complete mapping (motion §14).

---

## 12. Conversion — hand them the keeping

At t66 the visitor must understand: *this world was kept by someone, the keeping is the
product, and the map in front of me is where it happens* — and feel: *I want that goblin
at my table.* One action: **Join the Discord**.

- The board is a real authored map in product style — the film's last frame is the
  product's first frame, no cut (the morph is shipped grammar).
- Endcard per `copy-spec.md` direction C, lettered on the board, no box; entrance
  choreography as locked (wordmark → tagline write-on → subline → CTA last).
- The CTA performs the film's one taught rule: drawn at rest (graphite outline, paper
  fill, boiling offset border), **touch-lit** on hover/focus — amber blooming through
  the letterforms from the pointer side, contact shadow arriving with it. The visitor's
  first touch is the goblin's grammar, given away. Click: the die rolls a natural 20,
  new tab, `DISCORD_URL` (unset URL = button doesn't render).
- One quiet trace of the concept: the board carries faint edge-handling wear — this map
  has been *played on*. No pentimenti on the board itself (contrast + product truth
  outrank the theme at the conversion surface).
- Skip note from t16.5, replay valve, no analytics, nothing below the endcard.

## 13. Stage by stage — what changes vs `world.ts`, and the asset bill

Line refs are current v2 `world.ts` (4478 lines). "Kill" = retired; "keep" = geometry
survives, surface rebuilt; "new" = authored fresh.

**S1 — The Claim (t0–10.2).** *Today:* `buildAmbush` (1532–1766) + the infinite
`earthPlane`/`grassPlane` (2244–2254) + flat fills + hatch rock tone (1573).
*Changes:* the two planes die — camp island + cliff island with sculpted edges; genuine
night rig (skyDusk, fire as sole key, amber glow replacing `Film.tsx:100`'s hue); rocks
and cliff take baked tier tone + contours; adventurers re-surfaced silhouette-first;
bolt/arrow impacts as painted strokes. Watch the `camp` children-filter coupling
(1759–1763) when re-parenting. *Assets:* camp island, cliff island (shared S2/S7), fire
kit, camp kit re-surface, party trio re-surface, ember particles.

**S2 — The Address (t10.2–16.5).** *Today:* the freeze is the shipped curtain over v1
geometry; dust is nothing. *Changes:* flagship beat 1 — the cliff's underdrawing gets
construction ellipses, measure ticks, and **one erased, redrawn contour**; the grid
ghosts in; dust hangs as a graphite scribble sprite; his contact shadow is the frame's
only one. Tick tightened to ≤0.15t (closes P1-T3). *Assets:* cliff underdrawing marks,
dust scribble, the four me-line letterings (P6).

**S3 — Proof of Light (t16.5–26.5).** *Today:* `buildPathProps` (1802–2218) +
`buildGround`'s dressing (2225–2590) on the infinite planes. *Changes:* the path becomes
a ribbon island — the hero island's own bakes extended (albedo, bark, foliage, stroke
tiles); the seven prop beats keep their timeline but each prop gets its authored
surface + one whisper of history (older nail holes on the signpost, a graphite ring
where mushrooms grew last season); sign "letters" (2147/2189) become scribble rows; the
lantern beat is the thesis image — pool blooms, trees take their paint back, shadows
arrive with color; lantern staged so flame reads (P4d-T5 rule). *Assets:* path island
(the big build), lamppost restage, cave + door re-surface, chest re-surface, perch tree
+ ravens repaint, signpost, mushrooms, 40+ trees from the flora kit.

**S4 — Proof of Scenery (t26.5–36).** *Today:* `buildTheatre` (2593–2886), hatch tones
(2628/2670/2689/2759). *Changes:* the disc becomes a planked painted stage (floorboard
bake, kerb wear where the rope runs); forest half on visible radial rails; mountain flat
= reserved-paper snow; the freeze-flicker reveals graphite machinery — capstan,
counterweights, rails — and flagship beat 2: **scribed arcs worn into the under-disc**,
years of swings in one mark. Turn stays scrub-tied 1:1 with inertia. *Assets:* stage
disc re-surface, machinery set (new, graphite-only), rope (keep, re-surface), mountain
flat (new treatment), rails.

**S5 — Proof of Time (t36–50).** *Today:* `buildTavern` (2923–3390); crossHatch window

**Persistent interface.** Margin + ticks + chapter numeral + 66-tick ruler + skip note +
play/replay + © line, all DOM, per experience §4 — with the Hand's captions replacing
the Metamorphous divs (same element ids, or every `cap()` call silently no-ops —
`timeline.ts`'s missing-id early return). The ruler is the film's one self-referential
mark: passed ticks ink in — the page keeping its own record of your progress.

## 14. The goblin rebuild — the named complaint, answered

"The goblin looks like a bad asset drawing." The diagnosis, from the code: his *build*
is good (locked v2 design, real IK, the acting alphabet, `puppet.check` green) — his
*surface* is v1: flat fills plus three literal hatch patches (flank `world.ts:978`, jaw
`1211`, cloak tone `1366`) that violate the film's own first gate, and stroke shells
tuned for a smaller screen presence. The fix is surface and staging, not redesign:

1. **Remove every interior hatch** — the three patches above. Interior tone comes from
   the lit Lambert + a cloak gouache bake.
2. **Cloak as authored gouache** — a `bakeIslandAlbedo`-class bake: fold-following
   directional strokes, one direction per panel, committed shadow mass in the olive
   ramp, hem-edge drybrush wear (his own material tells his story: the most-worn cloak
   in the film).
3. **Face at hero polish** — amber eye as a real warm glint (the P4-T6/P5 lesson: the
   glint must survive the shipped framing; QA at ≥1920 and at phone width), skin in
   goblinGreen with the quiet pigment pass, expressions untouched.
4. **Presence budget** — the hero's measured floor becomes film law: at any acting beat
   the figure projects ≥100px of screen height on desktop (the P4d-T6 finding: at ~80px
   he was "a featureless olive dome"; at 105×110px he reads). Framing solves this, not
   scale changes — his world scale stays locked per beat sheet staging.
5. **Contour weight** moves off beaded hero-tier lines onto sketch shells (the P4e fix
   that made him read at the seam).
6. **Cloak hem follow-through** (hand-offset channel, puppet lane) — two frames of
   drag on the bolt and the leap, nothing elastic.

He is the only thing painted on both sides of the curtain, the only shadow in Prep, and
the loudest chroma in every frame by one deliberate step. After this pass he is also,
visibly, the best-kept asset in the film — which is the concept.

---

## 15. What this direction refuses

- No travelling seam through the film body: the hero's seam is the hero's; the film's
  two states swap by the tick, whole-frame, as the grammar catalog says.
- No desk, no frame-story furniture, no visible maker's hands, no fourth-wall workshop.
  The keeper is the goblin; the page is the only meta-surface.
- No evidence beat that captions itself, no camera that points at its own cleverness,
  no fifth flagship mark. Four, then discipline.
- No new copy, no lettered marginalia, no aging-yellow, no hatching (34 call sites
  retired by name), no ACES, no spinner, no unmotivated light.

The film's last argument is the direction's test: when *"I've built worlds for your DM
for years"* writes on at t58, the visitor should already believe it — because for eight
stages, the pixels kept the receipts.
